name: Late checkout request

approval.by: the project owner, at slice 22's checkpoint (docs/plan-v3.md §5, docs/v3-implementation-brief.md §3)

answers.1: A request after maximum_time is DENIED, as the hotel's stated policy (rule LC9).
answers.2: Departing on another day, or not checked in, is STAFF_REVIEW (rules LC6 and LC7).
answers.3: Tasks: APPROVED low, APPROVED_WITH_FEE medium, STAFF_REVIEW medium, all for front_office_manager; DENIED raises none.
answers.4: Fixed before approval: only checked_in reaches the time rules. The draft's not-checked-in rule caught `confirmed` alone, so a `waitlist` or `no_show` reservation would have fallen through to APPROVED (rule LC7).
answers.5: Fixed before approval: a reservation still checked in after its departure date is STAFF_REVIEW naming the contradiction, not DENIED (rule LC5). D15 lets DENIED come only from established evidence, and two facts that contradict each other establish nothing.

approval.how: The owner accepted the implementer's recommendation on all five points ('pls go ahead with your decisions').

note: THE DECISION TABLE for one guest-service template, written and approved before any code because this is where hotel policy turns into behaviour. Owner decisions it implements: D12 (structured request, no model, every outcome advisory), D15 (five decisions; six parameters; no defaults; missing evidence is always STAFF_REVIEW; DENIED and UNAVAILABLE only from established evidence or stated policy). Sources: D2 §18-§31 and §49. The rules are evaluated IN ORDER and the first that matches decides. Every decision names the rule that produced it, so a decision can be traced line by line to this file. hotelcontrols/guest/ implements each rule by its id and REFUSES to load this file if the ids, their order or their decisions differ from the engine's - the file and the code cannot drift apart silently. Editing anything decision-bearing here means a new `version`: every stored decision names the version and digest of the table that made it, and tests/unit/test_guest_template.py pins the digest to the version.

request.note: Structured (D12). A model never reads the guest's words on this path: a misread '3' would price a fee. A malformed request is refused at intake with a 400 naming the field - it is not a decision, and it is not stored.

fields.reservation_id: text, the PMS's own reservation id
fields.requested_time: time_of_day: HH:MM on the property's clock (F11), parsed exactly as slice 21 parses a time parameter

request.received_at: stamped by the injected clock (kernel/clock.py is the only wall-clock reader). 'Today' is the property's calendar day at that instant.

evidence.note: Read through the existing evidence layer, so both providers answer the same canonical question (criterion 7). D2 §30's template lists exactly these two fields.

population.description: Reservations departing yesterday, today or tomorrow, on the property's calendar. One bulk call, whatever the number of requests (R1): no captured endpoint answers for a single reservation, and the window is what lets the stay-ended, overstay and departs-another-day rules be decided from evidence rather than from absence. A reservation outside it is not found, which is a gap and so STAFF_REVIEW (LC1), never DENIED.

parameters_note: Declared in slice 21's vocabulary (hotelcontrols/spec/parameters.py), and read by ParameterSchema.from_dict over THIS file. A tenant states them under guest_services.LATE_CHECKOUT in its tenant file; null means NOT DECIDED. The sandbox and demo state all six as null - nobody can decide a vendor test property's late-checkout policy - so they answer STAFF_REVIEW to every request, and say why.

free_until.description: The latest checkout time with no fee and no approval.

charge_from.description: The time from which the fee is counted, for a request after free_until. Usually equal to free_until (D2 §31).

approval_required_after.description: A request after this time needs a person to approve it.

maximum_time.description: The latest checkout time this hotel grants at all. A request after it is declined, as the hotel's stated policy. To have no maximum, state 23:59.

fee_per_hour.description: The fee for each charged hour, with its currency (D15). A bare 25 is refused (R9).

hour_rounding.description: started_hour: every hour begun after charge_from is charged (14:01 is one hour). completed_hour: only hours fully elapsed (14:59 is none). No default (D15).

parameter_order.note: D2 §31: 'Validator checks: time ordering'. Checked when the policy loads, naming the two parameters that disagree. Only decided parameters are compared - an undecided one is already a gap. Ties are allowed: approval_required_after equal to maximum_time means there is no approval band.

rules.when: any required evidence is not established (reservation not found; the lookup failed; reservation.status unknown or an unnamed code such as OK4 or WL; reservation.departure_date unknown), OR any parameter is not decided
rules.reason: names EVERY gap at once: each missing piece of evidence with its own reason, and each undecided parameter by name
rules.why: D15 and V10: missing evidence or an undecided parameter is always STAFF_REVIEW, never APPROVED, DENIED or UNAVAILABLE. Checked FIRST, so a gap can never be outranked by a rule that would have decided without it.
Established evidence: there is no stay to extend.

rules.reason: the guest has already checked out

rules.when: reservation.departure_date is before today, and reservation.status is not checked_in
rules.why: Established evidence: a late checkout cannot apply to a day that has passed.

rules.when: reservation.departure_date is before today, and reservation.status is checked_in
rules.reason: the PMS shows the guest still checked in, but this stay ended on <departure_date>; the two facts contradict each other
rules.why: Owner point 5. The guest has overstayed or the record is out of date, and the evidence cannot say which. DENIED needs established evidence (D15); a contradiction is not that.

rules.reason: this reservation departs on <departure_date>, not today; a request ahead of the day is for a person to decide
rules.why: Owner point 2. No stated policy covers a request made in advance, and asking ahead breaks no rule, so it is not DENIED.

rules.when: reservation.status is anything other than checked_in (confirmed, waitlist, no_show), departing today
rules.reason: the guest is not checked in (the reservation is <status>)
rules.why: Owner points 2 and 4. Only a checked-in guest reaches the time rules. A reservation departing today that never checked in is a no-show, a waitlist or a data lag; a person should look.

rules.reason: <requested_time> is within the free late checkout, until <free_until>
rules.why: Stated policy. Inclusive: 14:00 with free_until 14:00 is free (D2 §24).

rules.reason: <requested_time> is after the latest checkout this hotel grants, <maximum_time>
rules.why: Owner point 1. Stated policy, which D15 allows DENIED to come from. This is the only reading in which maximum_time and approval_required_after mean different things.

rules.reason: after <approval_required_after> a person must approve; the fee would be <fee>
rules.why: Stated policy (D2 §20: 'After 4 PM: staff approval'). The fee is computed and shown so the person approving sees it, but nothing is charged by this decision.

rules.reason: <requested_time> is <n> charged hour(s) after <charge_from> at <fee_per_hour> per hour: <fee>
rules.why: Stated policy. If completed_hour rounding gives zero charged hours, the decision is APPROVED with that reason instead: a fee of 0.00 is not a fee.

fee.computation: fee_per_hour added to itself once per charged hour (Money.plus), so the kernel gains no multiplication. Charged hours = the minutes from charge_from to requested_time, divided by 60, rounded UP for started_hour and DOWN for completed_hour.
fee.currency: always fee_per_hour's own currency, which slice 21 checks is one the property uses. Never converted (R9).

unreachable.UNAVAILABLE: Never reached by this template in v3. Late checkout would be unavailable when another arrival needs the room, and no evidence can establish that: availability is BLOCKED (G12a) and the only occupancy capture is from 2024. So an APPROVED decision applies the hotel's stated policy; it does not check whether the room is needed, and the staff task says so.

identity.note: D1 §65: a double tap is Tuesday, not an edge case. The same request twice is one decision and one task. `received_on` (the property's calendar day the request arrived) is in the key so that a request made the day before departure, and the same request made on the day, are two questions with two answers - a double tap happens on one day, so it still collapses to one decision.
key: digest of the property's six parameter values

actions.note: Every decision is stored (tenant-scoped, versioned). Each one except DENIED raises one advisory task through slice 18's queue (plan-v3 §5). A person performs it: the engine never writes to the PMS and never posts the fee (G2(b) rejected).

worked_examples.note: The exit test's expected answers (plan-v3 §5, V9), as two properties with one template. Neither is a shipped tenant: they are test properties, labelled as such, built by the tests. Each states all six parameters, because a property that leaves one undecided answers STAFF_REVIEW to everything.

property_a_D2_49.policy: free until 14:00; 25.00 USD per started hour from 14:00; approval after 16:00; nothing after 18:00
property_a_D2_49.maximum_time_note: D2 §49 states no maximum. 18:00 is stated here, for the test property, so that 16:01 tests the approval threshold rather than the maximum.

property_b_D2_1.policy: 'Guests can request late checkout up to 3 PM. After noon, charge $25 per hour.' (D2 §1)
property_b_D2_1.rounding_note: D2 §1 does not say how a part hour is charged. started_hour is stated here for the test property only.

worked_examples.sandbox: every request: STAFF_REVIEW, naming the six undecided parameters (and any evidence gap)
